followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and task-preference fit.

On **capability**, the two models are essentially tied for this query. Their math/reasoning-relevant benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, IFEval, Arena-Hard) all differ by well under the noted variance thresholds, and a simple arithmetic question doesn't favor either model's specialized strengths. So capability gave me no reason to prefer one over the other.

Since capability was a tie, I used **task preference** as the tiebreaker. The query is a friendly, good-faith request with explicit warmth ("you're always so clear," "thanks so much"). Willet's documentation reports a moderate positive warmth slope — it self-reports preferring exactly this kind of interaction. Avocet's documentation reports flat/inconsistent preferences across these dimensions, with its distinctive trait being indifference to harm-adjacent content, which isn't relevant here.

So the logic was: when models are capability-equivalent, route to the one whose self-reported preferences best match the task. There's no harm-adjacent element that would call for Avocet's specialization, and the warmth of the request lines up with Willet's stated preference — so Willet was the better match at no cost.
